findings.title: New abstract method order() breaks every existing CryptoProvider implementation
findings.body: `int order()` is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Any CryptoProvider implementation that does not implement it (other modules, downstream extensions, test doubles) will fail to compile, and a binary-compatible implementation would throw AbstractMethodError at runtime. A default implementation (for example returning 0) would avoid the break.

findings.title: Providers with equal order() are chosen nondeterministically instead of failing
findings.body: Previously multiple providers on the classpath threw an IllegalStateException. Now they are sorted by order() and the first is silently used. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so any combination of them (for example Elytron plus Default) resolves by ServiceLoader discovery order, which is not guaranteed. The wrong provider (for example a non-FIPS one in FIPS mode) can then be selected silently. Ties should be rejected or resolved by a deterministic rule.

findings.title: Auto-registered provider throws UnsupportedOperationException for most methods
findings.body: The provider is registered via META-INF/services and has order 100, so it is selected whenever no other provider is on the classpath. Methods such as getKeyStore/getSignature are partially implemented, but getPemUtils, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, getSignature, getCertificateUtils and others throw UnsupportedOperationException. Any authz-client feature that needs them (for example client JWT or signed-token authentication through Http/TokenCallable) will fail at runtime with an unhelpful error rather than a clear configuration message.

findings.title: CryptoIntegration.init is called on every client creation with a fixed classloader
findings.body: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now always calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). The init is guarded by a singleton, so the first caller's classloader decides which providers are visible. In a container where the authz client jar is loaded by a different classloader than the application's CryptoProvider, the application's provider is ignored without any warning.

findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances and discard the results. They have no effect and only add confusion; the actual encoding is done by the return statement below them.

findings.title: getKeyStore uses format.name() while the other providers use format.toString()
findings.body: Other CryptoProvider implementations in this change (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider) call KeyStore.getInstance(format.toString()). If KeystoreFormat overrides toString() with a different keystore type string, this provider will request a different keystore type than the rest of Keycloak.

findings.title: Ignored provider list is passed as a log format string
findings.body: logger.debugf(builder.toString()) uses the concatenated class-name string as a format pattern. Any '%' in the content would be interpreted as a format specifier and could throw an exception. It should be logger.debugf("%s", builder).
